abstract: Background: Hematological traits are closely linked to immune and inflammatory processes implicated in thyroid dysfunction. Although observational studies have reported associations between blood-cell traits and thyroid disorders, whether these relationships reflect causal mechanisms remains unclear. Methods: We performed a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to investigate the causal effects of 25 genetically predicted hematological traits on hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from the UK Biobank. Independent single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were selected as instrumental variables and harmonized before analysis. Causal estimates were primarily obtained using the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method and complemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, simple mode, MR-PRESSO, and MR-robust adjusted profile score (MR-RAPS) analyses. Sensitivity analyses assessed heterogeneity, horizontal pleiotropy, reverse causality, and directionality. Significant findings were replicated using independent FinnGen summary statistics. Multivariable MR and Bayesian colocalization analyses were subsequently performed to investigate significant associations further. Results: Among the 25 hematological traits evaluated, eosinophil-related traits showed the strongest associations with hypothyroidism. Genetically predicted eosinophil counts were associated with an increased risk of hypothyroidism (odds ratio [OR] = 1.25, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.11-1.42, P = 4.0E-04, FDR = 0.002), while combined eosinophil-basophil counts showed similar associations (OR = 1.24, 95% CI: 1.10-1.40, P = 5.0E-04, FDR = 0.002). These findings were consistently replicated in FinnGen and remained significant after adjustment for basophil traits, body mass index, and C-reactive protein in multivariable MR analyses. No significant associations were observed for hyperthyroidism. Bayesian colocalization identified strong evidence of a shared genetic signal at the rs653178 locus on chromosome 12 (PP.H4 = 0.994). Conclusions: This study provides genetic evidence supporting a causal role for eosinophil-related traits in hypothyroidism susceptibility. The consistency of the findings across complementary Mendelian randomization approaches, independent replication, multivariable analyses, and colocalization strengthens the evidence that eosinophil-related immune mechanisms contribute to hypothyroidism susceptibility.
